device.manufacturer: Gree Electric Appliances (many OEM rebrands: Cooper & Hunter, etc.)
device.name: Gree Smart Air Conditioner (LAN)
device.notes:
Gree Wi-Fi air conditioners (and the many OEM rebrands) are controllable entirely on the LAN over a UDP/JSON protocol on port 7000 — no cloud, no account at any point. Gree is a very large manufacturer (active); the risk here is firmware churn, not abandonment: newer firmware moved from AES-ECB to AES-GCM ("encryption_version 2"), which older clients must handle.
TRANSPORT: UDP unicast + broadcast, port 7000. The JSON envelope carries fields t, i, uid, cid, tcid and pack; the pack is AES-128-ECB (PKCS-7), Base64-encoded. Two keys: a generic key shared by all devices (used for scan/bind) and a per-device key returned during binding.
FLOW:
  1. Discover: broadcast plaintext {"t":"scan"} to UDP 7000; each device
     answers with its MAC and an encrypted metadata pack.
  2. Bind: send a pack {"mac":"<MAC>","t":"bind","uid":0} (generic key); the
     device replies {"t":"bindok","mac":"<MAC>","key":"<per-device key>"}.
  3. Status: pack {"cols":["Pow","Mod","SetTem","WdSpd"],"mac":"<MAC>",
     "t":"status"} → values by parameter name (Pow, Mod, SetTem, TemUn, ...).
  4. Control: pack {"opt":["TemUn","SetTem"],"p":[0,27],"t":"cmd"}.

Newer firmware: some devices require encryption_version 2 (AES-GCM); a client should try AES-ECB first and fall back to GCM.

openness.notes: No official English protocol publication; tomikaa87/gree-remote documents it end-to-end and cmroche/greeclimate independently implements it (including the GCM firmware variant).

issued_to_client: Per-device AES key (from the bind exchange)
credentials.notes: Wi-Fi onboarding is app-mediated (not documented here). Control packs are AES-encrypted, but the generic key used for scan/bind is shared across all Gree devices, so binding is possible by anyone on the LAN.

factory_reset.effect: Returns the Wi-Fi module to onboarding (typically a remote-control key combination on the AC). The exact gesture varies by model and is not transcribed here.

methods.description: Join the AC's setup AP and hand it the home Wi-Fi credentials via the Gree onboarding flow; then discover it on the LAN (UDP 7000 scan) and bind to obtain the per-device key.

steps.action: Onboard the AC onto Wi-Fi (Gree+ app / its setup AP).
Broadcast {"t":"scan"} on UDP 7000 and bind to get the per-device key.
steps.expect: A bindok reply carrying the per-device AES key.

setup.notes: A factory-fresh AC hosts its own AP for Wi-Fi onboarding via the Gree+ app; local control needs no cloud. After the unit is on the LAN, the client performs the UDP bind (generic key → per-device key) once and reuses the per-device key. Wi-Fi onboarding wire steps are not documented here.

rejoin.notes: Wi-Fi re-provisioning is done through the module's onboarding, not the control protocol.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The UDP-7000 transport, the AES-ECB/Base64 pack scheme, the scan/bind exchange and the parameter names are from tomikaa87/gree-remote; the AES-GCM firmware split is from cmroche/greeclimate.
